literal: A spy, having spied, the information brought, even that, by another one spy, having verified, should confirm.
translation: Even the information brought by a spy who has investigated must be verified and confirmed through another independent spy.
modern: ஒரு ஒற்றன் ஆராய்ந்து கொண்டு வந்த செய்தியையும், வேறொரு ஒற்றனைக் கொண்டு ஆராய்ந்து உண்மை என்று உறுதி செய்து கொள்ள வேண்டும்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the necessity of cross-verifying intelligence in statecraft. A ruler must not act immediately on the report of a single spy, as there is always a risk of error, bias, or deception. Instead, the ruler should send a second, independent spy to investigate the same matter. Only when the information brought by the first spy is confirmed by the second spy should it be accepted as the truth. This double-check system ensures the accuracy of crucial state decisions.
